summary:
This week's news was mostly about who pays for the power, and the answer keeps shifting toward the data center owner, with exceptions.

In Arkansas, Entergy filed a second phase for Google's $4 billion West Memphis campus: 440 MW of solar, 1,400 MWh of batteries and new transmission, with Google paying the roughly $600 million cost and Entergy promising no bill increase. Neither has said how much power the campus itself will draw, so it isn't on our map yet. In Michigan, Google's 1 GW Van Buren Township campus won final site approval, with DTE service due in late 2027. In Wyoming, Black Hills disclosed earlier this month that it signed Google up through 2048 for the Cheyenne campus once tied to Crusoe's Project Jade, building 564 MW of new gas with Google's money. And in West Texas, Amazon's GW Ranch plans up to 7.65 GW of gas turbines off the grid entirely.

Louisiana is the counterexample. Reporting on Entergy's 10-plant plan for Meta's Hyperion campus says about $3.4 billion of the generation cost would be left for other customers after Meta's 20-year contract; regulators vote in December. Meta said it would sell up to $95 billion in stock to keep building.

Elsewhere, Dominion told Virginia it has about 12,000 MW of data centers under contract and a plan that could add more than $100 a month to residential bills over 20 years, backed by 14-year minimum-payment contracts so stranded costs fall on data centers. Amazon withdrew a Loudoun County proposal after neighbors objected, and AEP and Amazon agreed on early development of 960 MW of small reactors at a former Indiana coal plant, with a go-ahead decision expected by late 2029. For households, the details of each contract matter more than the headline megawatts.

projects.name: Stargate Abilene
projects.power: On-site natural gas plus grid power, including local wind (per Epoch AI)
projects.cost: not reported in the sources cited
projects.note: Partly operating: Epoch AI estimated four of eight buildings running in April, with completion projected for Q4 2026. A planned expansion toward 2 GW was dropped in March (see separate entry).

projects.name: Abilene Stargate expansion
projects.company: Crusoe (developer); Oracle and OpenAI (dropped); Meta reported in talks
projects.power: Not settled; DCD, citing The Information, reported power would not be ready at the site for about a year
projects.cost: not reported
projects.note: Oracle and OpenAI dropped plans to take the site from 1.2 GW to 2 GW (about 800 MW more); Nvidia reportedly paid Crusoe a $150 million deposit and courted Meta for the capacity, with no deal reported signed. A Stacker piece this week cited it as an example of the delays now hitting about half of planned capacity.

projects.company: Vantage Data Centers; part of the OpenAI/Oracle Stargate program
projects.power: On-site natural gas microgrid
projects.cost: more than $25 billion (as reported)
projects.note: Ten buildings planned; the first was expected online in the second half of 2026. Epoch AI put the Stargate share at 2 GW, above Vantage's 1.4 GW campus figure.

projects.cost: not reported in the sources cited
projects.note: Steel framing and roofing visible on the first building in April; projected completion Q4 2028 per Epoch AI.

projects.power: Natural gas microgrids with Bloom Energy fuel cells and batteries; El Paso Electric backup service was proposed and withdrawn
projects.cost: not reported in the sources cited
projects.note: On Oct. 13 Oracle pitched county commissioners a backup-power deal with El Paso Electric, plus up to $55 million a year in bill credits for three years, then withdrew it after commissioners said it tied the project to residents' bills despite promises it would power itself.

projects.company: Vantage Data Centers; OpenAI and Oracle
projects.power: We Energies; Oracle would pay for 125 to 250 MW from the Point Beach nuclear plant under an extended NextEra contract
projects.cost: $15 billion (as reported)
projects.note: Oracle's Oct. 2 offer to buy Point Beach power, which it says would save We Energies customers about $300 million in fuel costs over 2027-2033, awaits Wisconsin PSC approval; data centers are now a bipartisan campaign issue in the state.

projects.name: Hyperion
projects.power: Entergy Louisiana: three gas units approved in 2025 and seven more proposed, for ten in all (754 MW each, about 7.5 GW as reported), with batteries and transmission
projects.cost: Entergy's estimates for the new generation are reported at $12.9 billion and about $13.6 billion; Meta's regional investment over $50 billion (as reported)
projects.note: The seven-plant request goes to a Louisiana PSC vote in December (Dec. 16 per earlier reporting); The Lens reports about a quarter of the generation cost, roughly $3.4 billion, would be left for other customers after Meta's 20-year contract, while an Earthjustice appeal of the PSC's decision to shield Meta's figures is in state court. Meta on Oct. 26 said it would sell up to $95 billion in stock, largely to fund campuses like this one, which it plans at 5 GW.

projects.name: Prometheus
projects.power: Grid (AEP Ohio area); Meta's disclosure this week did not detail the power mix
projects.cost: not reported
projects.note: Meta said the first phase is live, with hundreds of thousands of GPUs and a plan to scale to about a gigawatt and roughly a million GPUs; 1,000 MW is the planned scale, not current draw.

sources.title: Meta details Ohio Prometheus data center campus, with first phase live

projects.name: Colossus 2 and Southaven sites
projects.power: On-site gas turbines in Southaven (41 permanent turbines permitted in March to replace 27 unpermitted ones) and Tesla Megapacks
projects.cost: more than $20 billion for the Mississippi facility (as reported)
projects.note: Mississippi regulators are seeking about $6.1 million in stormwater-permit penalties across three sites, and a federal judge refused the Justice Department's bid to end the NAACP's turbine lawsuit. The 2 GW figure is Musk's total for Colossus training compute, not a utility-filed load.

projects.name: Homer City Energy Campus
projects.company: Homer City Redevelopment with Kiewit; Amazon Web Services (tenant)
projects.power: A 4.5 GW natural gas plant on the former coal plant site
projects.cost: not disclosed (as reported)
projects.note: AWS filed plans this month for 36 buildings on 1,100 acres, with data center construction in four stages from December 2026 to 2036. 4,500 MW is the gas plant's size; a campus load hasn't been reported.

projects.name: Susquehanna campus
projects.power: Up to 1,920 MW from Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant under a 17-year PPA, moving from behind-the-meter to grid-connected retail service
projects.cost: PPA notionally $18 billion (as reported)
projects.note: Deliveries ramp to 840-1,200 MW by 2029 and the full 1,920 MW by 2032; the original 300 MW behind-the-meter setup was to be reconfigured during a spring 2026 refueling outage.

sources.title: Talen, Amazon Launch $18B Nuclear PPA—A Grid-Connected IPP Model for the Data Center Era

projects.name: Project Rainier
projects.power: Indiana Michigan Power (AEP) for Phase I; NIPSCO for Phase II
projects.cost: $11 billion Phase I plus $15 billion Phase II (as reported)
projects.note: Phase I has run since October 2025 and Phase II was slated to start in 2026; the profile cited gives conflicting counts of buildings live.

projects.name: Fairwater
projects.power: We Energies
projects.cost: $4.7 billion of Wisconsin construction spending 2024-2028 (as reported)
projects.note: The first building went live in June, a second is due in 2028 and 15 more were approved in January. Microsoft hasn't published a load; 450 MW is a tracker site's estimate.

projects.name: Paducah AI campus (DOE site)
projects.company: Brookfield (developer); NextEra Energy (power); no tenant named
projects.power: NextEra-built generation of up to 2 GW of grid-connected gas and 2.6 GW of batteries; Big Rivers Electric wholesale, Jackson Purchase Energy retail
projects.cost: $100 billion (as reported)
projects.note: Up to 1.8 GW of utility capacity for more than 1.2 GW of compute on the former uranium enrichment plant; the project has become the issue in the Nov. 3 county judge/executive race, where the challenger wants a community benefit agreement.

projects.name: Project Matador (HyperGrid)
projects.company: Fermi America with Texas Tech University System; TensorWave (tenant); AMD (credit support)
projects.power: Mostly behind the meter: gas turbines first, with four AP1000 reactors under NRC review, plus solar, wind, batteries and grid power
projects.cost: not reported; TensorWave lease up to $6.5 billion over 15 years (as reported)
projects.note: NRC staff's draft environmental review preliminarily favors a license for four AP1000 reactors, with comments due Nov. 23 and a final review targeted for December; the first 222 MW building (facility power) for TensorWave, backed by AMD credit support, is due in the second half of 2027. Fermi has cited 11 GW and, more recently, nearly 17 GW, and its cofounders have left the company.

sources.title: Fermi America, Blue Energy make strides in Texas

Fermi America acquires 600MW of gas turbines for 11GW AI mega campus in Amarillo, Texas

projects.name: Project Jade
projects.company: Google (customer); Black Hills Corp. (power); Crusoe exited in June
projects.power: Black Hills: up to 590 MW of grid service (564 MW of new gas at Cheyenne Prairie plus 26 MW of market power), and management of about 2.1 GW of third-party resources through a private microgrid; total resource mix about 2.7 GW
projects.cost: $1.8 billion for Black Hills' new gas generation; Google advanced $399 million (as reported)
projects.note: Black Hills disclosed Oct. 6 that it signed agreements through 2048 to serve Google's planned Cheyenne data center, with service from late 2027 and peak load in 2030; Bloomberg had reported in June that Google was the customer behind Crusoe's 1.8 GW Project Jade, though Black Hills' filing doesn't use that name. Four approvals are still pending, and Black Hills says the deal keeps costs off other customers.

projects.name: Alton Steel site campus
projects.power: Grid-connected through Ameren Illinois, with TerraWatt paying for local upgrades
projects.cost: not disclosed
projects.note: New this week: up to 1 GW in 200 MW blocks on a former steel mill, contingent on rezoning and an Ameren study; first block late 2027 to early 2029 and no tenant signed.

projects.company: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers
projects.power: 500 MW under the city agreement with an option for 500 MW more; natural gas available for behind-the-meter generation
projects.cost: not disclosed
projects.note: Taylor's council unanimously approved an economic development agreement this month; construction 2027-2029 with first power in the first half of 2028.

sources.title: 1 GW Data Center Project Advances Near Austin

projects.name: El Paso data center
projects.power: El Paso Electric via McCloud Generation, 366 MW of modular gas units next to the site paid for by Meta, as a five-year bridge from 2027
projects.cost: not reported
projects.note: Meta's request grew from 220 MW to over 440 MW by 2027 and possibly 1 GW by 2029; 1,000 MW is that upper figure, and the plant stays off EPE's transmission system with long-term cost recovery left for later.

sources.title: Meta funds El Paso nat gas plant as interim power fix

projects.name: Project Cannoli
projects.power: DTE Electric under contracts approved by the Michigan PSC on Oct. 1; Google to fund up to 1,600 MW of renewables and 480 MW of batteries; DTE has also proposed about 2.1 GW of new gas in Milan and Handy townships
projects.cost: not reported; DTE's proposed gas plants estimated at $6.4 billion combined (as reported)
projects.note: The township planning commission gave final site-plan approval in mid-October; service is due in December 2027 with full load by December 2028. Regulators haven't ruled on DTE's proposed gas plants, and the PSC meets again Nov. 5.

sources.title: Google data center wins final approval in Wayne County: What residents need to know

projects.name: GW Ranch
projects.company: Pacifico Energy (developer); Amazon (owner of the data center buildings)
projects.power: Off-grid at first: up to 7.65 GW of on-site gas turbines (35 units), up to 750 MW of solar and 1.8 GW of batteries, designed to connect to the grid later
projects.cost: about $12 billion per the developer's February estimate (as reported)
projects.note: 7,650 MW is the on-site gas plant's size; a data center load hasn't been reported. Amazon filed permits in August for three 189,000-square-foot buildings after the state permitted the turbines in January; because it runs off the grid, its cost doesn't land on ERCOT customers' bills.

sources.title: Amazon Discloses Ownership of GW Ranch, Giant Texas Data Center-Gas Power Complex

changes: Meta Hyperion: reporting puts Entergy's plan at ten 754 MW gas plants, with about $3.4 billion left for other customers; an appeal over Meta's sealed figures is in court; PSC vote in December.
Project Jade (Cheyenne): Black Hills signed Google through 2048: up to 590 MW of grid service plus a 2.1 GW private microgrid, $1.8 billion of new gas.
Fermi Matador: NRC draft environmental review preliminarily favors the four-reactor license; comments due Nov. 23.
Added: Google's 1 GW Project Cannoli in Van Buren Township, Michigan (final site approval).
Added: Amazon's GW Ranch in Pecos County, Texas: up to 7.65 GW of off-grid gas.
Not added: Google's West Memphis campus got a $600 million Google-funded second phase from Entergy Arkansas, but no load has been reported.
